title: Healthy Boundary Setting
shortDefinition: The psychological limits, guidelines, and rules that a person creates to identify safe, permissible ways for other people to behave towards them.
dailyExample: Saying: 'I want to support you, but I don't have the emotional capacity to discuss this topic tonight. Can we reconnect on Saturday?' instead of silently resenting them.
psychologyTheory: Pioneered across systemic family therapy and psychodynamic models. Boundaries are not punitive; they are self-preservational parameters that prevent burnout and enmeshment.
inTherapy: We work through the guilt of saying 'no', differentiate porous vs. rigid vs. healthy boundaries, and practice low-conflict scripts.
practicalTakeaway: Setting a boundary will often disappoint people who benefited from your lack of boundaries. Their temporary discomfort does not mean you did something wrong.
